answer: An identity registers by posting a 600-unit copper bond and a hardware credential whose serial number the registry records once. Forging N identities locks 600N units, and a proven sybil cluster is slashed 80 percent of every bonded identity it contains. Splitting a bond across aliases is unprofitable because each alias pays the full marginal cost and shares the slashed penalty, while independent jurors cross-check the relic and comet attestations.
